newsitem.title: BARBADOS: Clinton about ready to cast away crutches.
newsitem.headline: Clinton about ready to cast away crutches.

text.p: President Bill Clinton on Monday was close to casting away his crutches and moving to a pair of walking canes as he moves into the next phase of his recovery from March 14 knee surgery, the White House said.
"He's ready to get some freedom of movement back and would like to ditch the crutches," said White House spokeswoman Mary Ellen Glynn.
She said Clinton conferred with his doctors and his physical therapist as well as first lady Hilary Rodham Clinton on Sunday at poolside to talk about his condition and when he could move to a cane.
The president, wrapping up a week-long trip to Mexico, Costa Rica and Barbados, was to depart Barbados and arrive back in Washington later on Monday.

Clinton was to use a pair of carved, wooden canes given to him at the San Francisco monastery in Tlaxcala, Mexico, last week. Clinton took a few steps with them when he received them. The canes have since been outfitted with rubber tips.
"They're ready to go whenever he feels that he can get around on them," Glynn said.
Clinton tore a tendon in his right knee during a late-night stumble at the Florida estate of golfer Greg Norman on March 14. He underwent surgery the same day to repair it.
The president in recent days has suffered back pain and Glynn said the doctors believed the crutches might be aggravating his back.

"The doctors are anxious to get him off his crutches. They think that may be in part causing some of his back pain. When you're putting extra stress on your back and changing the way you move around, that can put a lot of stress on you," Glynn said.
During his weekend in Barbados, Clinton got into the swimming pool for some physical therapy at the Heron Bay estate where he stayed.
Clinton set a grueling pace during the longest foreign trip he has taken since hurting the knee, but Glynn said one day of rest at poolside did much to rejuvenate him.
